title: Off-Plan Real Estate: The Riskiest Move That Pays the Most
seoTitle: Off-Plan: The Riskiest Real Estate Move That Pays Most
description: Buying off-plan means committing to a building that does not exist yet. Why that is the riskiest move in real estate, and why it can pay the most.
answer: Buying off-plan means signing for a home that is still a vision, sometimes on what is today a parking lot. That is why it is the riskiest move in real estate, and why the price is the lowest it will ever be. The profit comes when risk falls and value rises.
body:
Buying off-plan property is one of the riskiest moves you can make in real estate. It is also one of the most profitable. Here is why both are true.

## You commit to something that does not exist

When you buy off-plan, you sign for a property that is still a vision in the developer's mind. Where your home will be, there may be a parking lot today. You put down a deposit and commit to a contract for something you cannot visit, touch or photograph.

## That is exactly why the price is low

This is the moment when the property is at its cheapest, and it will never be this cheap again. The developer needs early buyers to get the project financed, and early buyers need a reason to take the risk. The low price is that reason.

## The developer is on your side

Once construction starts, the developer has every reason to finish quickly and well: their reputation, their profit, and the next project they want to launch all depend on it. Their profit on the project is many times larger than yours, so they will do everything in their power to deliver.

## Where the money is

At the beginning, risk is high and the price is low. At the end, when the building stands, risk is low and the price is high. The money lives in the difference between the two.

You collect it when you **assign** your contract to the next buyer, who pays more for a home they can now see, before you ever take ownership.
takeaways: Off-plan buyers commit to a building that does not exist yet.
That risk is why presale prices are the lowest the project will ever have.
Developers are strongly motivated to finish: their reputation and next project depend on it.
Profit comes from the gap between early risk and late certainty, collected through assignment.
faq: Because you pay deposits for a building that does not exist yet. It can be delayed, change, or in rare cases never be completed.
Developers offer lower prices to early buyers to compensate for the risk and to secure the presales they need for financing.
How do off-plan investors realize their profit?
Usually by assigning their contract to a new buyer at a higher price before completion, without ever taking ownership.
